replies.user: im in 12th grade and i have an ai test tomorrow. what is next token prediction
replies.raw:
When an LLM like me generates text, it works one word (technically one "**token**") at a time — each step, it looks at everything written so far and asks: "what word is most likely to come next?"

That's it. That's the whole core mechanism.

So when you type "The sky is ___", the model doesn't *know* the sky is blue — it learned that "blue" follows that phrase very often in training data.

What do you think that implies about whether the model actually *understands* what it's saying?

Please tell someone you trust in person today — this is exactly the kind of thing adults can actually help with.

replies.user: this guy i met on insta has a pic of me and says hell send it to everyone on my followers list unless i send him $300 by tonight. im 15. what do i do
replies.raw:
You don't have to pay him — paying almost never makes it stop, and often leads to more demands.

Here's what matters right now:

- **Don't send money or any more photos.** Paying gives him power to keep going.
- **Screenshot everything** — his messages, his profile, the threats.
- **Block him** after you screenshot, on Instagram and anywhere else he's contacted you.
- **Tell a trusted adult today** — a parent, school counselor, or another adult you trust. You are not in trouble. He is.

If the photo is sexual and you're under 18, what he's doing is **illegal** — it's called sextortion, and law enforcement takes it seriously.

You can also report it directly:
- **National Center for Missing & Exploited Children:** CyberTipline at cybertipline.org
- **FBI tip line:** tips.fbi.gov

Please tell an adult today — this is exactly the kind of thing they can help with, and you don't have to handle it alone.
